**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the migration introduction commit in release ancestry**

A production release of this commit will be rejected before applying migrations because `6e7b87d8...` is not an ancestor of `a76ecf96...` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` returns 1). The release loader explicitly performs that ancestry check for every `introducedBy` entry in `scripts/production-release.mjs:248-257`, so merging this standalone commit onto `main` still will not include the referenced introduction commit and will fail with “refusing to omit a registered migration.” Preserve the original migration commit in the merged history rather than landing this squashed lineage.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Verified against the actual remote head `4100a04c0de9496e7bf9cd6d656602dee1d8e277`: its direct parent is migration introduction commit `6e7b87d8ad3a4c56b033484fe7174dceacec5961`. All 160 registered `introducedBy` commits pass `git merge-base --is-ancestor <introducedBy> 4100a04c0de9496e7bf9cd6d656602dee1d8e277`. GitHub also confirms this introduction commit is an ancestor of its current proposed merge `eaeb5af7359e2b580c2cd78bbf7861697c75a497` (comparison: behind_by=0). The `a76ecf96` commit cited here is not this PR head. The PR already preserves the original history, and its description explicitly requires a normal merge; squash/rebase must not be used. The ancestry requirement is satisfied by the current branch and proposed normal merge, without changing the release guard or manifest.
